Title: Brent breaks US$100 on Mideast flare-up, fanning inflation fears
Article:
HONG KONG: Brent broke above US$100 a barrel Wednesday as oil prices surged and stocks struggled on the back of a fresh flare-up in the Middle East crisis, putting upward pressure on inflation ahead of key US data at the end of the week.
With the US-Iran conflict now in its seventh month and showing no sign of calming despite White House claims of an imminent deal, investors are growing increasingly anxious that the Federal Reserve will have to hike interest rates to cap surging consumer prices.
The two foes are locked in a stalemate, with Tehran maintaining a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for the world's oil and gas, and Washington pushing a campaign to choke the Islamic republic's ports and economy.
Iran said Wednesday it had struck a US military base in Jordan following American attacks on its vessels in the strait, which itself was in retaliation for ballistic missile launches at a US warship.
Tehran also said it would target oil tankers off Kuwait and Bahrain and urged crews to leave their ships, according to the IRNA state news agency.
That came after Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen exchanged strikes, with the rebels targeting oil facilities in an offensive towards the Red Sea's Bab al-Mandab chokepoint.
The waterway is an increasingly important route for Saudi oil with the Strait of Hormuz shut.
Both main crude contracts jumped more than one percent, with Brent hitting as high as $100.19, the highest since July. West Texas Intermediate was heading towards $95 for the first time since June.
The surge in energy costs has kept inflation elevated globally and is putting pressure on central banks to hike borrowing costs, with the European Central Bank tipped to do so Thursday.
All focus is on the release of the US consumer price index Friday, which is seen as the key to whether the Fed lifts rates next week or not.
"The continuing conflict in the Middle East is keeping concerns over supply disruptions, and that in turn is worrying investors about the inflationary consequences of elevated oil prices," said Fawad Razaqzada, a market analyst at FOREX.com.
"For the Fed, the combination of resilient US employment and renewed pressure from energy prices are both hawkish signals.
"A sustained rise in oil prices would risk reversing the progress on inflation that policymakers have been relying on to justify lower interest rates, while simultaneously squeezing consumers and businesses."
The prospect of borrowing costs heading up is weighing on equities, with all three main indexes dropping on Wall Street.
Asian markets fluctuated, though tech firms continued to enjoy a recovery from July's rout as the AI boom returns to the fore.
Seoul led the gainers as chipmaker SK hynix rallied more than three percent.
Shanghai, Wellington, Taipei, Bangkok and Manila also advanced, though Hong Kong, Tokyo, Sydney, Singapore, Mumbai and Jakarta were down.
London, Frankfurt and Paris fell at the open.
On currency markets, the yen strengthened to around 152.95 per dollar after seeing Tuesday's rally -- which saw it within a whisker of its 2026 high -- pared towards the end of the day.

Title: UK rejects Israel's 'damaging' sanctions retaliation
Article:
LONDON: British foreign minister Ed Miliband on Wednesday condemned as "regrettable and damaging" Israel's decision to order the  closure of the UK's consulate in Jerusalem as retaliation for London-led Western sanctions over settler violence.
"We anticipated this might happen because we saw other countries, the Dutch, for example, who had announced sanctions, who had seen these reprisals from Israel.
"I think they're regrettable and damaging," Miliband told BBC Radio.
Israel on Tuesday ordered the closure after 12 countries including Britain, Canada and France announced they would sanction trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, following a surge in settler attacks against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Israel said it would also expel British representatives at a centre monitoring the US-brokered ceasefire plan in Gaza, bar British training for Palestinian Authority forces and ban 12 Britons, mostly members of parliament, from visiting the country.
Miliband rejected suggestions that the sanctions would impact intelligence cooperation with Israel.
"We have important intelligence and security relationships with Israel, and I'm confident they will continue," he said, declining to go into details.
"And I was very clear yesterday that we do believe in working with our Israeli partners when it comes to the threats they face from Iran," he added.
Miliband also dismissed the criticism of the sanctions by Britain's chief rabbi.
Ephraim Mirvis on Tuesday called the measures "little more than political flag-bearing."
He said it was a "truly a dark day for British Jews", predicting that the measures "will succeed only in bolstering the very extremism they seek to target."
Several antisemitic attacks in London this year have targeted synagogues and other Jewish sites.

Title: TH: Haj offer letters for 31,600 prospective pilgrims to be issued from Sept 21
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will begin issuing haj offer letters to 31,600 prospective pilgrims for the 1448H/2027 haj season in stages from Sept 21.
TH reminded selected prospective pilgrims to ensure that they have a minimum balance of RM15,000 in their accounts with the institution to qualify for the offer letters, besides being required to pass a medical examination.
In addition, TH will begin organising Haj Basic Courses at more than 200 mosques nationwide from Sept 25 to help prospective pilgrims prepare in terms of knowledge before performing the pilgrimage.
"Prospective pilgrims are advised to update their personal information and check their haj turn through THiJARI or at the nearest TH branch," TH said in a statement.
It also said the early confirmation of the official quota of 31,600 pilgrims by the Saudi Arabian government would give prospective pilgrims ample opportunity to plan their financial and health preparations, as well as gain the necessary knowledge in line with the concept of istito'ah (ability).
For the 1448H/2027 haj season, TH is maintaining the haj cost at RM33,300 per person for Muassah pilgrims for the fourth consecutive year, despite facing inflationary pressures, global economic uncertainties and rising service costs in the Holy Land.
In addition, TH is continuing the targeted Haj Financial Assistance (HAFIS), involving an allocation of about RM234 million for this season, bringing the cumulative amount borne by TH since HAFIS was introduced in 2001 to more than RM2.8 billion.
For B40 pilgrims who receive government assistance such as Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR), the haj payment is set at RM15,000 (45 per cent of the haj cost), after taking into account HAFIS of RM17,300 and special government assistance of RM1,000 per person.
M40 prospective pilgrims, meanwhile, will be required to pay RM23,500, with HAFIS assistance of RM9,800 (29 per cent), while T20 pilgrims with an individual monthly income of at least RM15,000 will have to pay the full haj cost of RM33,300 per person.
Meanwhile, TH chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain said the success in maintaining the cost structure and providing HAFIS was achieved through efficient governance, early planning, strategic negotiations and the signing of long-term contracts with service providers.
He said TH's ability to maintain the cost structure, provide HAFIS and improve the quality of its services was driven by the institution's increasingly stronger financial position.
He said this position was achieved through disciplined financial management, enhanced risk management and continuous improvements in governance practices.
On the official quota,  Rashid said the early confirmation provided prospective pilgrims with ample opportunity to plan their financial and health preparations, as well as gain the necessary knowledge in line with the concept of istito'ah.
Meanwhile, TH Group managing director and chief executive officer Mustakim Mohamad said almost 90 per cent of the haj cost was related to accommodation, flights and services in the Holy Land.
"TH succeeded in maintaining the haj cost by containing increases in flight costs through five-year long-term contracts to manage the risk of price fluctuations in the interest of pilgrims. The major challenge now is the increase in oil prices and supply costs following the conflict in the Middle East," he said.
He said TH had also managed to reduce the rental costs of new, higher-quality hotels through direct negotiations, thereby containing the impact of rising inflation and the costs of new services or facilities in the Holy Land.
"This achievement is important for TH because it is not merely about maintaining the figures, but about how we plan ahead, manage risks and leverage TH's operational efficiency to provide the best value to pilgrims," he said.

Title: Court of Appeal overturns RM50,000 defamation award granted to Guan Eng
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today overturned a High Court ruling that had ordered former housing and local government minister Datuk Zuraida Kamaruddin and two others to pay RM50,000 in damages to DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng for defamation.
A three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril, Datuk Ahmad Kamal Md Shahid, and Datuk Amarjeet Singh unanimously allowed the appeals filed by Zuraida, MalaysiaNow editor Muhammad Abd Ar-Rahman Koya and MNow Media Sdn Bhd.
The panel also dismissed Lim's cross-appeal, which had sought an increase in the damages awarded and ordered him to pay RM30,000 in costs.
Delivering the panel's unanimous decision, Justice Mohd Firuz said the article in question did not carry the defamatory meaning as alleged by Lim.
"We find that there were obvious errors in the judgment of the High Court and the judgment cannot stand," he said, adding that the manner in which the High Court dealt with the defence was purely unsatisfactory.
Justice Mohd Firuz observed that the court's final analysis revealed the High Court's assessment of the defence of justification had been grounded solely in documentary evidence, without regard to the actual exchanges that took place between the two ministers during their meeting.
He also pointed to inconsistencies in the High Court judge's findings, noting that while she had found malice in one part of her ruling, she had simultaneously held that there was no evidence of malice in another.
The legal proceedings began on June 7, 2024, when Lim, a former Finance Minister, filed a defamation suit at the Shah Alam High Court, naming Zuraida, Muhammad Abd Ar-Rahman Koya and MNow Media as defendants.
In his statement of claim, Lim alleged that Zuraida had made false statements concerning him in relation to a housing project for former plantation workers in Bestari Jaya, Selangor.
In March this year, the High Court ruled in his favour, finding that the statements made against him were defamatory and awarding him RM50,000 in damages.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/03/1390638/lim-guan-eng-wins-defamation-suit-against-zuraida-two-others
Zuraida and the two other defendants subsequently appealed against the High Court's decision, while Lim filed a cross-appeal challenging the quantum of damages awarded.
During the appellate proceedings, Lim's counsel, Datuk Sankara Narayanan Nair, contended that the RM50,000 awarded by the High Court was insufficient, arguing that prevailing trends in case law warranted an award of RM250,000.
However, the lawyer representing Zuraida and the two other appellants, Nizamuddin Abdul Hamid, submitted that the comments made by Zuraida, which were published by MNow Media, were not defamatory in nature, and urged the Court of Appeal to set aside the High Court's ruling.
Following the decision, Sankara told the media that he would seek instructions from his client on whether to pursue the matter further before the Federal Court.

Title: 7 more Taman Manggis PPR units sealed, residents left scrambling for shelter
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Seven more Taman Manggis People's Housing Project (PPR) units were sealed yesterday, days after Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow defended the sealing of five other units.
This brings the total number of sealed units to 12, according to Taman Manggis PPR residents' association chairman Pannir Selvam.
He said affected residents were scrambling for temporary accommodation, with some seeking shelter in budget hotels.
Pannir said residents received notices last November and were informed that action would be taken this month, but claimed some were not given adequate notice before their units were sealed.
"One resident received a call asking her to return home from work because her unit was going to be sealed. She had not received any further notice," he said during a gathering outside the PPR late last night.
Pannir said those affected included low-income earners, an elderly woman with eyesight problems and families facing financial difficulties.
He said one evicted resident, whom he described as an orphaned man, had nowhere to go.
He also questioned the relocation of residents from the island to housing schemes in Seberang Prai, including Desa Wawasan, Mak Mandin and Ampang Jajar.
"Why does the state government want to move everyone from the island to the mainland?" he asked, citing higher transportation costs for residents working on the island.
Pannir said residents were not opposed to leaving Taman Manggis if suitable alternatives were provided.
"At least offer them a house they can buy so they can move out. The rest of the B40 group cannot afford to buy a house, so the state government must find a solution for them," he said.
He said some residents had lived at Taman Manggis since 2004 and expected the units to eventually be offered under a rent-to-own (RTO) scheme.
Pannir claimed residents were initially told they would rent the units for two years before being considered for RTO, but the arrangement did not materialise after a change in the state government in 2008.
He also cited a 2019 announcement that Taman Manggis residents would be given priority for housing projects in Jelutong and Balik Pulau, saying this had yet to materialise.
[[nid:1529066]]
Pannir claimed repeated requests for discussions with the Penang Housing Board and the state housing executive councillor had gone unanswered.
He said some residents were being displaced before replacement homes were ready.
One affected resident, Wahidah Ismail, who has lived at Taman Manggis since 2005, said she was now staying separately from her husband and three children after her unit was sealed.
She claimed her appeal against the eviction had received no response.
Wahidah said the reason cited involved the unit being registered under her late father-in-law's name and an allegation that her mother-in-law owned a house, which she said had been sold decades ago.
Pannir urged the state government to assess each household before further evictions.
"This is not about refusing to leave. We just want the government to study each family's situation before evicting them," he added.
He claimed more residents were at risk, but the association had not been given the full list.
Parti Sosialis Malaysia (PSM) had recently urged the state authorities to halt evictions at Taman Manggis PPR, while the Penang Housing Board defended the action.
The Penang government said enforcement action against the affected units was not carried out abruptly, but followed cross-checks, detailed assessments, engagement sessions and the issuance of notices in accordance with established procedures.
It said the PPR scheme was intended as transitional housing for low-income B40 families, allowing them to rent units at heavily subsidised rates while stabilising their finances.

Title: Manila defence boss slams 'bullying' China after note at forum
Article:
SEOUL: The Philippine defence chief has accused Beijing of "bullying", alleging he was handed a Chinese note at an international forum that asserted China's expansive claims over contested waters.
Secretary Gilberto Teodoro was on stage for a panel discussion at the Seoul Defense Dialogue on Tuesday when he received a paper from what appeared to be an event staffer, video shows.
"I have a note here. I think this is from China," he said, before reading out its contents in the South Korean capital.
"China's position on the South China Sea arbitration is clear, consistent, and firm.... The arbitration violates fundamental principles of international law," he said, reading from the note.
The mention of arbitration refers to a landmark 2016 ruling by an international tribunal in The Hague that overwhelmingly sided with the Philippines in its case against China's claims to the South China Sea.
Multiple nations in the region, including the Philippines, have territorial claims that overlap with China's, and altercations occur regularly in the heavily patrolled waterway.
Neither South Korea's defence ministry, which organised the forum, nor the Chinese embassy responded to AFP's requests for comment on Teodoro's allegation.
The Philippine defence chief lambasted the note, arguing it was an act of aggression.
"If this is a Chinese position sent to me, it not only disrespects international law," he said, but also the forum host and "the rest of the audience here."
"So, perhaps basic decency and behaviour is what China needs to do... This is actual coercion, bullying, and aggression," he said, noting he would keep the memo as a "momento of how desperate China is."
Yonhap news agency reported a military attache at China's embassy in Seoul asked an event staffer to hand over the note. AFP has not been able to confirm that account.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesian wildfire emissions surge to world's highest, data shows
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia is facing a surge in emissions from wildfires burning through parched stretches of forest and peatland on the islands of Borneo and Sumatra, with carbon dioxide readings currently the highest in the world, data showed on Wednesday.
Fire emissions from Indonesia from September 1 to Sept 7 reached 19.7 million metric tonnes, overtaking Russia this week and making up more than a third of the global total, according to Fire Emissions Watch, a portal developed by the European Union's Copernicus climate monitoring service.
Indonesia is one of the world's most fire-prone countries, but as "super-El Niño" weather conditions drive up temperatures and cause punishing droughts, the country is battling what authorities say is its most intense wildfire season in 11 years.
"We do expect to see some fires across the region at this time of year, but with El Niño, it clearly just gives a big enhancement to them," said Mark Parrington, senior scientist at the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service in Bonn.
"It's much drier, it's hotter, and when there's ignition, these fires burn in a far more extreme way."
From Sept 1 to Sept 7, fire emission intensity exceeded 1,500 kg/sq km, more than 10 times the Russian level, with the highest concentrations in Kalimantan in Indonesia's part of Borneo and eastern parts of Sumatra, Copernicus data showed on Wednesday.
Emissions were 273 per cent higher than the seasonal average, though still lower than the 21.7 million tonnes emitted in the same week of 2015, when Indonesia was battling similarly intense El Nino conditions.
Among the hardest hit areas has been the city of Pontianak in West Kalimantan, where the air quality index was 394 on Wednesday, according to Swiss air quality monitoring firm IQAir.
A reading of 300 is considered hazardous.
Indonesia's environment ministry told Reuters in a statement that it viewed the hazardous air quality readings in Kalimantan and elsewhere "with concern."
It said it was monitoring Copernicus's data, but added it "does not directly reflect air quality conditions in a specific area", and other factors needed to be taken into account.
From January to July this year, fires burned around 202,000 hectares of Indonesian land, about a third the amount over the same period in 2015, said Nisa Novita of the environmental group YKAN, which helps communities tackle fires.
"However, August data are estimated to show a significant increase of around 600,000 hectares, particularly in Kalimantan, Sumatra and South Papua," she said.
Indonesia lost a total of 2.6 million hectares to fire in the whole of 2015, an area bigger than Wales.
The number of recorded hotspots from Aug 1 to Sept 8 reached 13,443, compared to 9,454 over the same period of 2015, according to Indonesian forest ministry monitoring platform Sipongi, based on data from NASA's Terra and Aqua satellites.
A record monthly high for hotspots was recorded in October 2015, Sipongi data showed.
Fire Emissions Watch uses satellite observations to estimate concentrations of particulate matter, volatile organic compounds, greenhouse gases and other fire-fuelled pollutants, but Parrington said it could actually be underestimating the extent of the problem.
"One of the aspects with peat fires is if they're burning at low temperatures or underground, they'd be below the detection limit of the sensors, which means we're not actually seeing them," he said.
Studies have shown that fires in Indonesia in 2015 produced more emissions per day than the whole of the EU, and caused more than 100,000 excess deaths throughout Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore.
"We have to remember that this is still the beginning of the season, and we expect the fires to continue and the emissions to keep increasing, potentially through to the end of October, which is what we saw in 2015," said Parrington.
"In two months we'll know how extreme this year has been, but the early indications are that it is at pace, if not slightly above those previous El Nino years."

Title: [UPDATED] Azeez chose to wear lockup attire, handcuffs in court, says MACC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim chose to appear in court wearing a police lockup uniform and handcuffs despite being advised that he did not have to do so, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said.
In a statement today, the anti-graft agency said Azeez's appearance in the purple police lockup attire and handcuffs when he was brought to the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to face charges was entirely at his own request.
MACC said that before he was taken to court, its officers, accompanying police personnel and Azeez's lawyer had advised him to change into ordinary clothes.
He was also informed that there was no requirement for him to be handcuffed.
"However, he insisted on remaining in the lockup attire and handcuffs until the process of reading the charges was completed," the commission said.
The MACC stressed that Azeez's decision to wear the lockup attire and handcuffs was not made on the instructions or at the request of any party, particularly the commission.
It also urged the public not to speculate or spread inaccurate information over the matter.
The clarification comes amid scrutiny over the treatment of suspects brought to court, following the MACC's recent decision to discontinue the use of its
orange lockup attire
for suspects appearing in court for remand proceedings.
It was reported that MACC has suspended, with immediate effect, the requirement for persons under investigation to wear its orange uniform when brought to court for remand proceedings.
The move comes after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said on Sept 4 that political leaders would be given leeway not to wear the MACC orange uniform when brought to court.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman had said the decision was made following recent developments and current recommendations concerning procedures for handling persons under investigation, particularly when they are brought to court.
"Persons under investigation will be allowed to wear their own clothes when brought to court, while lock-up attire will only be worn throughout the period they are held in the lock-up," he said in a statement today.
Abd Halim said the use of handcuffs would depend on the circumstances of each case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man, 5 juveniles charged over rape, gang rape of 15-year-old girl
Article:
KANGAR: A man and five minors were charged separately in the Sessions Court and Magistrate's Court here today over the rape and gang rape of a 15-year-old girl last July.
Before Sessions Court judge Sharifah Norazlita Syed Salim Idid, an 18-year-old unemployed man was charged with raping the 15-year-old victim at a house in Simpang Empat here at 2am on July 18.
The accused was charged under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which upon conviction carries a maximum sentence of 20 years' imprisonment and caning.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor Mohd Alif Farhan Hassan, while the accused was represented by lawyers Mohamad Alif Farhan Mohamad Supian and Zuhair Ahmad Zakuan.
The court allowed the accused to be released on bail of RM7,000 with one surety, and ordered him to report to the nearest police station at the beginning of each month until the case is concluded. He was also barred from interfering with the victim and prosecution witnesses.
The case was fixed for mention on Oct 9 for the document submission process.
Meanwhile, at the Magistrate's Court, five male juveniles aged between 15 and 17 pleaded guilty to charges against them as read before Magistrate Ana Rozana Mohd Nor.
According to the charge sheets, all five juvenile offenders were charged with gang-raping the same victim at the same location on two separate occasions.
The first incident was allegedly committed by two of the accused between 3am and 4am on July 18, while the second incident involved four of the accused between 2am and 5am on July 19.
All the juveniles were charged under Section 375B of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum sentence of 30 years' imprisonment.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor Alia Suzila Chek Pi, while all the accused were represented by lawyer Wan Nursyaheedah Wan Najmi.
The court allowed all the accused to be released on bail of between RM500 and RM1,000 each.
The court fixed Oct 7 as the next mention date for the submission of conduct reports and the presentation of case facts before sentencing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malicious prosecution: Shahrir's suit against three resolved, Thomas pending
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The civil suit filed by Tan Sri Shahrir Samad against former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Latheefa Koya, the commission and the Government of Malaysia over alleged malicious prosecution has been amicably resolved at the High Court here.
However, the suit against former Attorney General Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, the first defendant, remains pending, with the court fixing Oct 16 to hear Shahrir's application for leave to discontinue the action against him.
Shahrir's counsel Datuk Firoz Hussein Ahmad Jamaluddin told High Court Judge Gan Techiong that his client had reached a resolution with the second to fourth defendants.
"Accordingly, we withdraw with no liberty to file afresh and no order as to costs. The parties have also agreed that no statements will be made regarding this suit.
"In respect of the first defendant (Thomas), we will be filing an application for leave under Order 21 Rule 3(2) of the Rules of Court 2012 to discontinue the suit," he said.
Senior federal counsel Zureen Elina Mohd Dom, appearing for the three defendants, confirmed the agreement.
Judge Gan then ordered Sharir's claims against Latheefa, the MACC and the government to be
struck out
without liberty to file afresh and with no order as to costs.
The court also directed Shahrir to file the application for leave to discontinue the suit against Thomas within seven days and fixed Oct 16 to hear the application.
Shahrir and Thomas were present in court.
On Monday, the court adjourned proceedings until today to allow the parties to continue discussions on a possible resolution. Shahrir had been scheduled to continue his cross examination by Thomas's counsel Alan Adrian Gomez.
The former Johor Baru member of Parliament filed the civil suit against the four defendants in December 2023, alleging malicious prosecution.
The suit arose from the RM1 million cheque Shahrir received from former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak for rehabilitation works on the Puri Langkasuka housing project in Larkin, Johor.
In 2020, Shahrir was charged with failing to declare to the Inland Revenue Board the RM1 million in income allegedly received from Najib. The High Court acquitted him of the charge on Jan 5, 2023.
Thomas, who served as Attorney General from June 2018 to February 2020, denied Shahrir's allegations against him, including abuse of power, describing them as "indefensible".
He maintained that he had resigned as Attorney General on Feb 28, 2020, while Shahrir's criminal trial only began on July 26, 2022.

Title: Azeez posts RM450,000 bail after being charged with using position to secure chairmanship
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim emerged from the lock-up in purple remand attire and handcuffs to facilitate the RM450,000 bail process after claiming trial to using his position to secure a lucrative company chairmanship.
The 60-year-old former Baling member of parliament was immediately mobbed by photographers and videographers who had been waiting for him since 7am.
He was surrounded by policemen as he made his way to the bail payment counter, where two family members stood as bailors.
Azeez, who appeared calm, simply said he was doing well and nodded when asked for comment.
The bail process was completed in less than five minutes.
Azeez was then brought through a back entrance and is expected to be handed over by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to police to facilitate investigations under a two-day remand order pursuant to Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
Earlier, Azeez claimed trial to using his position 12 years ago to secure the post of chairman of Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, which carried an annual remuneration of RM690,000.
According to the charge, Azeez, as TH chairman, used his position to secure the chairmanship, which came with an annual salary of RM690,000 and the use of a BMW 7 Series with a full-time driver.
He allegedly instructed TH chief executive officer Tan Sri Ismee Ismail to nominate him as TH's representative in Putrajaya Perdana Bhd.
He is also accused of persuading board members during the TH Board of Directors Meeting No. 4/2014 (309) to approve a proposal to invest up to RM193.5 million, representing up to 30 per cent of the existing issued share capital, in Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, in which he had an interest.
He is charged under Section 23(1) of the MACC Act, punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act.
The section provides for a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the value of the gratification or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-KPTM administrator charged with 6 offences involving female students
Article:
IPOH: A former Kolej Poly-Tech Mara (KPTM) administrator here was charged with six offences involving alleged use of criminal force against two female students and obscene words against four others.
Roykarnaen Maseri, 44, pleaded not guilty to all charges when they were read separately before magistrates S. Punitha and Norizan Riduan in two separate courtrooms here today.
In the first courtroom, Roykarnaen was charged with intentionally using criminal force against a 19-year-old female student with the intention of outraging her modesty by pulling her arm towards her shoulder, placing his hand on her waist and kissing her forehead.
The offence was allegedly committed at an activity room at the college at 6.15pm on Aug 6.
On the second charge, he was accused of intentionally using criminal force against a 22-year-old female student with the intention of outraging her modesty by touching her waist, pulling her by the waist and attempting to kiss her on the mouth.
The offence was allegedly committed at the same place at 6.12pm on Aug 5.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Muhammad Zulqarnain Wan Asmira prosecuted, while lawyer Aiman Rusli represented the accused.
The two charges were framed under Section 354 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of up to 10 years, or a fine, or whipping, or any two of those punishments, upon conviction.
In a separate courtroom, Roykarnaen was charged with using obscene words against four female students, aged between 18 and 20, with the intention of causing, or knowing that such communication was likely to cause, harassment, distress, fear or anxiety.
The offences were allegedly committed at a house in Halaman Meru Impian, Jelapang; inside a car in the Silibin area; and at the college's activity room between June 18 and Sept 6.
The charges were framed under Section 507B of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of three years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Zarris Sofea Zainudin prosecuted, while Aiman represented the accused.
During mitigation, Aiman urged the court to grant his client lower bail, saying Roykarnaen had been unemployed since last month and needed to support his 72-year-old father, who has diabetes and high blood pressure, and his 58-year-old mother, who has arthritis.
He said his client also had a 7-year-old daughter and a wife, had no previous criminal record and had cooperated with police during investigations.
The court set bail at RM8,000 for all six charges with one surety and ordered the accused not to contact or interfere with the victims and witnesses until the disposal of the case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Capital A's Teleport 1H revenue jumps 35pct on e-commerce demand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Teleport, the logistics arm of Capital A Bhd, recorded a 35 per cent year-on-year increase in revenue to US$156.4 million in the first half of 2026 (1H26), driven by continued e-commerce demand.
Its net operating profit more than doubled to US$2.7 million from US$700,000 a year earlier, while earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation rose 15 per cent to US$12.1 million.
Profit after tax stood at US$3.1 million, with the second quarter marking Teleport's fourth consecutive profitable quarter.
The Southeast Asian e-commerce logistics specialist said growth in e-commerce demand drove higher volumes and margins during the period.
Total cargo volume increased 18 per cent year-on-year to 182,660 tonnes, while the number of parcels moved nearly doubled to 118.2 million from a year earlier.
Teleport said its performance also outpaced the broader regional market.
In Southeast Asia, its volume grew 34 per cent in 1H26, nearly three times the regional market growth of 12 per cent.
Across Asia Pacific, Teleport's revenue increased 26 per cent and volume rose 12 per cent, compared with declines of three per cent in revenue and five per cent in volume for the wider Asia Pacific air cargo market.
Teleport chief executive officer Pete Chareonwongsak said the company's asset-light, hybrid network had enabled it to maintain volume growth despite disruptions caused by volatile jet fuel prices and instability along Middle Eastern air cargo routes.
"As cargo volumes continue to scale across our network, the benefits of scale are coming through at the profit lines and holding across quarters," he said.
For the second half of 2026, Teleport plans to deploy US$50 million in growth capital ahead of the seasonal e-commerce peak, focusing on expanding third-party airline capacity and opening new routes.
These include China-Middle East services through its Bahrain hub, Asia-Oceania connectivity, Penang-Europe services via the Maldives and China-Philippines routes.
"This further enhances the Teleport Network's flexibility and agility to maintain the durability of our operational capability in a challenging market," Pete said.
He said non-AirAsia belly capacity accounted for 44 per cent of Teleport's total revenue in the second quarter, highlighting the growing contribution from its multi-partner network.
Teleport's hybrid capacity mix comprises AirAsia belly space, 55 partner airlines and dedicated freighters, providing the company with operational flexibility amid market disruptions.
Volume moved using third-party capacity grew seven per cent year-on-year in 1H26, while utilisation of its dedicated freighters jumped 89 per cent.
Teleport also expanded its airline partnerships, including a new capacity agreement with MASkargo for Phnom Penh, an extension of its general sales agent contract with Turkish Cargo out of Kuala Lumpur and additional Myanmar Airways International freighter capacity in Yangon.
Its network currently covers more than 290 cities across 80 countries in Asia Pacific and beyond.
According to WorldACD, Teleport ranks first in Southeast Asia and ninth in Asia by cargo volume.

Title: [UPDATED] Malaysia ready to send assets to fight Indonesia fires, awaits Indonesia's approval
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia is ready to send assets to help Indonesia tackle forest fires contributing to the haze, pending confirmation and approval.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and the Foreign Ministry had informed the cabinet that Malaysia had prepared a list of assets to assist Indonesia.
"However, so far there has been no confirmation on any form of cooperation to use Malaysian assets to help put out the fires.
"We have extended (the offer) through the embassy and the Foreign Ministry, while Nadma has also made the necessary preparations," he told reporters at the weekly press conference here today.
Asked about preparations for next week's Malaysia Day celebrations in Sarawak amid the haze, Fahmi said the main event in Kuching would be held indoors at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching, with more than 5,000 people expected to attend.
He said several other programmes planned at various locations in Sarawak would go ahead, although their locations could be adjusted depending on the situation.
"In Kuching, for example, the exhibition for the Malaysia Day celebrations will be held at Plaza Merdeka, within the building, so that members of the public can view the exhibition without having to spend a long time outdoors.
"We also note that the haze situation in Sarawak currently appears to be improving slightly.
"However, everything remains subject to weather conditions, as well as hotspots and open burning, particularly in neighbouring countries," he said.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said
Asean needs to review the existing mechanisms
for dealing with transboundary haze to avoid adverse impacts on people's health.
He said Asean ministers need to pay serious attention to the matter as the haze can have a direct impact on the health and lives of the people, especially children and babies.

Title: Zara inquest: Psychiatrist explains assessment of diary entries, informants
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Consultant forensic psychiatrist Dr Chua Sze Hung told the Coroner's Court today that he had considered the positive aspects of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir's diaries in his assessment.
The recalled witness said there were moments of casual interaction between the deceased and her friends.
"Otherwise, most of the diary's contents were descriptions about her life in school. The reason why the diaries were listed in such a way is so that I can assist the court and show what psychological constructs actually brought about the risk factors.
"Yeah, I did consider the positive side of it as well," he said in response to a question from Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan.
Asked whether he had analysed in percentage terms whether the positive or negative aspects were more common and whether this had any impact on his assessment, Dr Chua said it would be counterproductive to assign a numerical score in psychology and psychiatry.
"It will be counterproductive to actually assign a numerical score when it comes to psychology and psychiatry, because we need to understand the nuances and the descriptive understanding of that person's psychological construct and context.
"I would say that there were multiple vulnerabilities that were prominent to me, like what I have listed. The trauma and pain described were significant in my opinion, especially when it comes to a point where the deceased was wishing death upon herself and others. So yes, I have taken these factors into consideration," said Dr Chua.
The Coroner then questioned whether the positive aspects were reflected in Dr Chua's report.
Court: But in all fairness to the deceased as well, you didn't put any remarks or comments about the positive sides in your report, is that correct?
Doctor: I did include one or two parts of it, which I described the adjustment to the new environment and the new dynamic of it, but not overall.
Dr Chua was also questioned about possible bias or distortion in accounts provided by informants.
He said two types of reliability were taken into account when examining accounts from proxy informants: extrinsic and intrinsic reliability.
On extrinsic reliability, Dr Chua said multiple sources would be sought, as far as possible, to corroborate an account. If information came from only one source, this would be noted.
For intrinsic reliability, he said the structure of a person's narrative would be examined, including its logical structure, unstructured presentation, admission of a lack of memory, superfluous content and unexpected complications in the narration.
"Of course, it will not be possible to eliminate 100 per cent of the bias," he said.
Asked whether he knew that some of the peer informants were under
investigation
over the incident, Dr Chua said he became aware of this as the interviews progressed.
Zara was found unconscious on the ground floor of her school hostel on July 16, 2025, and was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital.

Title: 'Where's daddy?': Pilot's daughter longs for father killed in heli crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "Mommy, daddy will be back tomorrow, right? Sofia misses daddy. Why are there so many people with us?
"Sofia, mommy and daddy love Sofia. Mommy still hopes that daddy will come home. We have to stay strong. All of mommy's children are strong."
Those were among the heartbreaking messages posted by the wife of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq, Izzati Syamimi, on Threads after learning that her husband was among five people confirmed dead in a helicopter crash at STOLport Long Lellang, Sarawak, yesterday.
Earlier, the mother of two had also uploaded two other posts asking the public to pray for her small family and that everything would be made easier for them.
"Please pray for me and the children. Pray for my husband, my angel in heaven.
"I have never felt pain like this... please come home."
The posts were also accompanied by a screenshot showing her husband's last known location.
In her latest post this morning, Izzati also appealed to the media to give her some space as she coped with the difficult time.
In the incident yesterday afternoon, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including its pilot, crashed near Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport), Ulu Baram.
The helicopter was operating a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) flight to the interior of Sarawak.
However, air assistance from the police air base in Kuching could not be deployed yesterday due to hazy weather and because
permission to fly had not been granted
by the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM).
This morning, more than 20 personnel from various agencies, including 12 firefighters, were deployed for the search and rescue (SAR) operation.
Marudi Fire and Rescue Station chief Assistant Fire Superintendent Jessbent Jenus said the team was scheduled to depart at about 9am using a Fire and Rescue Department Mi-171 helicopter.
The journey by road from Marudi to the crash site is estimated to take about 10 hours.

Title: Rapid KL to replace Kelana Jaya line track in stages from Sunday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rapid KL will carry out track replacement work on the Kelana Jaya Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) in stages covering seven phases, starting Sept 13 until next September.
Rapid KL in a statement today announced that the improvement work is being carried out to ensure the track infrastructure is always at a high level of safety and reliability.
According to the statement, stations involved in the track replacement work will begin operating at 9.30 am compared to the usual 6 am, while stations not involved will operate as usual according to schedule.
The track replacement work involves Gombak and Taman Melati stations on Sept 13, 20 and 27, followed by the second phase for Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum stations (Nov 15, 22 and 29), as well as the third phase covering Dato' Keramat, Jelatek and Setiawangsa stations (Jan 10, 17 and 24, 2027).
The fourth phase involves Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum stations on 14, 21 and 28 March 2027, followed by the fifth phase involving Masjid Jamek, Dang Wangi, Kampung Baru, KLCC and Ampang Park stations on 9, 16 and 23 May 2027.
Meanwhile, the sixth phase involves Taman Jaya, Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum stations on 11, 18 and 25 July 2027, while the final phase involves Gombak and Taman Melati stations on 12, 19 and 26 Sept 2027.
Ticket machines at each station involved will be temporarily closed until 9.30am and users can obtain tickets at the station counters while Rapid KL and Touch 'n Go product users can continue their journey as usual.
Rapid KL will also provide a free shuttle bus service connecting the stations involved during the track replacement works.
To facilitate passenger movement, station staff, auxiliary police and 'Prasarana Troopers' volunteers will be stationed at the affected locations, while signboards and information leaflets will also be provided.
Kelana Jaya Line users are advised to check the track replacement work schedule and alternative bus movements via the website www.myrapid.com.my and Rapid KL's official social media channels.

Title: [UPDATED] Dengue cases surge 66pct, deaths nearly double
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Dengue cases have risen by 66 per cent as of epidemiological week 35 this year compared with the same period in 2025.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said 65,979 cases had been recorded this year, compared with 39,616 cases during the same period last year.
"There were 32 dengue-related deaths as of epidemiological week 35 in 2025, compared with 62 during the same period this year, representing an increase of 93.8 per cent," he told reporters at the weekly press conference here today.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said, the Housing and Local Government Ministry would hold large-scale gotong-royong programmes, including in areas identified as red zones or where outbreaks had occurred.
Fahmi said the cabinet was also briefed on the progress and success of the Wolbachia mosquito breeding programme, including in Putrajaya.
"However, the cabinet was informed that when fogging is conducted, the Wolbachia mosquitoes, which can prevent the virus from reproducing and spreading in Aedes mosquitoes, are also killed.
"One of the matters discussed was the need to step up efforts to carry out large-scale gotong-royong activities, including in areas identified as red zones or where outbreaks have occurred," he said.

Title: [UPDATED] Cabinet extends condolences to families of Long Lellang helicopter crash victims
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has extended its condolences to the families of five people killed in yesterday's
Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash
in Long Lellang, Sarawak.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) was investigating the incident and would submit its findings to the Cabinet.
"We do not yet know what caused the incident. We leave confirmation of the circumstances and the investigation to CAAM.
"The Health Minister has informed us that all five victims have been identified and their next of kin have been notified," he told a press conference here today.
In the incident yesterday, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport), Ulu Baram.
The helicopter was operating a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) flight
providing crucial medical services
to the deep interior of Sarawak.

Title: Woman seeks help to find husband missing since Sept 6
Article:
KULAI: A woman is desperately seeking help to locate her husband, who has been uncontactable since Sept 6, leaving their children pining for their father.
Mohammad Nazrizal Basiron, 32, last spoke to his wife by phone at 8.29pm that day.
She claimed that during the call, her husband told her he had been detained by an unidentified person, while she could hear several other voices in the background.
She said the call was then cut off and all attempts to contact him afterwards were unsuccessful.
She said Nazrizal was travelling from Saleng to Bandar Tenggara in Kota Tinggi to pick up her and their children when he went missing.
She said the children had been asking about their father and hoping for his return.
She appealed to the public to contact her if they had any information about her husband, who was driving a white Toyota Avanza, registration number BPR 871.
He was last seen wearing a red Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) jersey.
Meanwhile, district police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee confirmed that a police report was lodged on Sept 7.
He said Bandar Tenggara police were investigating the missing person report.

Title: Mikro MSC to acquire cable manufacturer Broadguard for RM30mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mikro MSC Bhd is acquiring Broadguard Sdn Bhd for RM30 million to expand its business into the wholesale and distribution of cables and related products used in security and surveillance systems.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, the company said the acquisition will complement its existing electrical and electronics (E&E) business, broaden the group's product and customer base and provide access to Broadguard's customer and supplier network.
Mikro has signed a share sale agreement to acquire the entire equity interest in Broadguard, to be satisfied via the issuance of 51.72 million new shares at about 58 sen each to Broadguard shareholders Sie Chee Din and Wong Meng Jie.
Sie will receive RM24 million worth of shares, while Wong will receive RM6 million worth.
Upon completion, Broadguard will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Mikro.
Broadguard, incorporated in 2004, is principally involved in the wholesale of cables and related products for security systems.
Its revenue rose to RM17.62 million in the financial year ended April 30, 2026 (FY26) from RM14.80 million a year earlier, while profit after tax increased to RM2.15 million from RM1.39 million.
The vendors have also provided a three-year profit guarantee, under which Broadguard's audited profit after tax will be at least RM2 million for FY26, RM2.25 million for FY27 and RM2.5 million for FY28.
Mikro said the RM30 million purchase price was arrived at on a willing-buyer, willing-seller basis, taking into account an independent valuation by Asia Equity Research Sdn Bhd, which valued Broadguard at between RM27.67 million and RM30.80 million.
The new shares represent about 4.28 per cent of Mikro's existing issued shares, while the issue price of about 58 sen represents a 2.5 per cent discount to its five-day volume-weighted average market price of 59.49 sen.
The acquisition is not expected to have a material effect on Mikro's consolidated earnings and earnings per share for FY26.
Mikro expects to submit its application to Bursa Malaysia within two months, with the acquisition targeted for completion in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Title: Pas backs political funding bill in principle, seeks more details
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas supports the proposed Political Financing Bill in principle, saying it is necessary to uphold the democratic system and safeguard the rights of political parties.
Its deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man, however, said Pas needed more details on the proposed bill before making a final decision on its position.
"Basically, we agree that political financing should be implemented to ensure the democratic system is respected and the rights of every political party are protected.
"We need detailed information regarding the bill. Several discussions have been held and the party will make a decision at its next central working committee meeting," he said when contacted.
Tuan Ibrahim, who is also Perikatan Nasional deputy chairman, urged the government to ensure that no foreign funds were channelled to any political party to prevent foreign interference in the country's political affairs.
He said safeguards against foreign funding should be included in the proposed legislation to protect the country's political sovereignty.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said yesterday said
all 72 registered political parties
had been urged to submit their positions in writing on the proposed Political Financing Bill.
She said official responses from each party would provide a clearer picture of whether they supported or opposed the bill, or had alternative proposals.

Title: TNB Genco continues investing in fleet reliability, renewables and storage pipeline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: TNB Power Generation Sdn Bhd (TNB Genco) continues to invest in the reliability of its existing generation fleet while advancing its renewable and storage pipeline, including a hybrid hydro-floating solar project combining 595 megawatts (MW) of floating solar with 1,190 megawatt-hours (MWh) of battery storage, targeted for completion in 2028.
The RM1.96 billion project is located at the Tasik Kenyir Dam in Terengganu. Upon its completion, the facility is slated to become the largest floating solar power plant in Southeast Asia.
"As Malaysia's largest power producer, TNB Genco plays a central role in shaping the country's energy mix," said TNB Genco's managing director Datuk Shahrir Abdul Latiff.
Hence, TNB Genco's transformation strategy focuses on three parallel tracks, namely sustaining the reliability of existing generation assets, developing renewable and storage capacity to support the energy transition, and building capability in emerging technologies for the longer term.
The approach reflects TNB's broader commitment to advancing Malaysia's energy transition while safeguarding the reliability the nation depends on.
"Reliability and sustainability should be pursued as complementary objectives rather than competing priorities, consistent with TNB Genco's approach to maintaining system dependability while progressing the transition to cleaner energy infrastructure," he said at the International Sustainable Energy Summit (ISES) 2026 recently.
Shahrir spoke at the session entitled "Pioneering the Future: Next-Gen Renewables and Clean Fuels", where he represented TNB Genco alongside representatives from Sarawak Energy, Malakoff Corporation Berhad and the ASEAN Centre for Energy.
Among others, the session examined the pathways required to scale emerging clean energy solutions, including technology readiness, system integration, commercial viability, as well as the policy and investment frameworks necessary to move these solutions from innovation to widespread deployment.

Title: Zara's diaries 'most critical, uncontaminated premortem data', court told
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The late Zara Qairina Mahathir's own written diaries, documenting various difficulties, represented the "most critical and uncontaminated premortem data", the Coroner's Court heard today.
Consultant forensic psychiatrist Dr Chua Sze Hung said this while testifying before coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan.
During examination-in-chief, Dr Chua was asked about consultant psychiatrist Dr Simon Wong devoting a section of his report to a "Psychiatric Assessment of the Mother", based on an interview on Jan 5 this year, almost six months after Zara's death.
Asked whether an assessment of a surviving parent was a proper substitute for assessing the deceased adolescent's mental state, Dr Chua replied: "No."
"In the context and framework of psychological autopsy, assessing the mother is not needed. The focus is to assist the court in determining the manner of death of the deceased, and the way forward is a psychological autopsy.
"An assessment of the surviving parent is not a proper clinical or methodological substitute for a retrospective assessment of the deceased adolescent's mental state.
"In forensic psychiatry, attempting to swap the two represents a category error, a clinical mismatch that mixes up two different subjects, timelines, and psychological realities. These are two distinct clinical subjects," he said in response to conducting officer Nahra Dollah.
Dr Chua said Zara's timeline was retrospective and pertained to the manner of death, while the assessment of her mother, conducted nearly six months after the incident, evaluated the mother's current mental state.
"A cross-sectional psychiatric diagnosis or non-diagnosis of the mother's current mental state is of little help in understanding the adolescent symptom load and final suicidal intent," he said.
Dr Chua also said forensic literature warned that survivors in death inquiries could be interested parties whose recollections could be coloured by guilt, anger and shame.
Zara, 13, was found unconscious on the ground floor of her school hostel on July 16, 2025, and was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
The inquest, which began on Sept 3, 2025, has heard testimony from various witnesses, including students, teachers, police officers, forensic pathologists, psychiatrists and forensic document examiners.

Title: Umno strengthens digital machinery with AIRA ahead of GE16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno is expanding the use of its artificial intelligence assistant AIRA as part of a wider effort to strengthen the party's digital machinery ahead of the 16th general election (GE16).
Umno Information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said AIRA had already been used during the Sabah and Negri Sembilan elections to help candidates and the public obtain information and clarification about issues and candidates.
She said the platform was particularly useful in introducing new candidates who were less well known to voters in their constituencies.
"AIRA was first introduced in the Sabah election, and we found that it helped candidates and the community obtain clarification about the candidates we were presenting, especially new candidates who were not well known to voters in the state constituencies," she said.
She made the remarks at the Umno Information Recognition Ceremony today, held in conjunction with the Umno general assembly.
Also present were Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail, secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan.
The Pengerang member of parliament said AIRA, or Artificial Intelligence Rakyat Assistant, was developed by Umno's Information Department in collaboration with the Umno Patriotic School.
She said the platform would continue to be developed as part of efforts to modernise the party's information machinery and respond more effectively to issues emerging online.
Azalina said Umno was also strengthening its grassroots digital network by establishing more Digital Secretariats at division and branch levels from 2026 to 2027.
She said members would undergo regular training to equip them to respond to issues and correct misinformation and allegations against the party.
"Courses will be conducted so that our members have the skills and ability not only to respond, but also to correct various allegations directed at our party," she said.
She said digital engagement, including likes, shares and comments, had become an important part of Umno's information strategy, with the approach showing results during elections in Sabah, Johor and Negri Sembilan.
She said the party's digital initiatives would help strengthen its grassroots reach and better prepare members to engage voters and address issues online ahead of GE16.

Title: Six civil servants among 11 remanded over vehicle document falsification
Article:
IPOH: Eleven people, including six civil servants, have been remanded to assist investigations into an alleged syndicate involved in submitting falsified documents for vehicle ownership transfers.
The suspects, comprising seven men and four women aged between 30 and 40, were brought before magistrate Norizan Riduan today.
Norizan allowed the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC)'s application to remand the suspects from today until Monday.
The remand was sought to facilitate investigations under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009.
The suspects, who were brought to court in MACC vehicles, arrived at the complex at 9.15am and were taken away at 11am.
Yesterday, the suspects, comprising five agents and six Road Transport Department (RTD) personnel, were arrested at 10pm while giving their statements at the Perak MACC office.
A source said the suspects had conspired to submit falsified documents to the RTD for vehicle ownership transfers involving 16 registration numbers.
"Initial investigations found that the offence took place in 2025, with the agents suspected of conspiring with civil servants to submit the falsified documents.
"The documents were believed to have been used to facilitate vehicle ownership transfers illegally," the source said.
