Title: Malaysian woman nabbed at Delhi airport with RM2.24mil worth of ganja
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian woman was arrested at Indira Gandhi International Airport in India on Friday after she was caught with more than 15kg of ganja worth 52.5 million rupees, or about RM2.24 million.
The woman had arrived at Terminal 3 from Kuala Lumpur before she was identified through passenger profiling.
"An inspection of a trolley bag she was carrying revealed 30 plastic packages containing a substance suspected to be ganja," Delhi Customs said in a statement.
The woman was detained while the drugs were seized under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act.
The case is being investigated under Sections 8, 20, 23 and 29 of the same act, covering the illegal import of drugs, as well as abetment and criminal conspiracy. The offences carry jail terms and fines.
Indian authorities have yet to disclose the identity or age of the woman.
Delhi Customs has also not disclosed details on the origin of the ganja, who handed the drugs to the suspect, or who was supposed to receive them in India.
It remains unknown whether the woman was paid to carry the drugs. Investigations are ongoing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Protesters urge South Korea to stay out of Iran war
Article:
SEOUL: Dozens of South Koreans urged their government on Wednesday not to deploy troops to the strategic Strait of Hormuz, slamming what they called Washington's "illegal war."
The protesters across from the large US embassy compound in Seoul waved signs saying "Do not join a war of aggression" as their leaders weigh a "contribution" to the waterway's security.
US President Donald Trump has pressured ally South Korea to help in the Middle East war, which has seen Iran take a stranglehold on the strait key to global oil supplies.
"We cannot send our young people into a sea of death!" chanted the protesters, who numbered about 60 according to an AFP estimate, on the steps outside Seoul's Sejong Center for the Performing Arts.
The protest came a day after South Korean defence authorities said they had sent a fact-finding mission to assess the situation in Hormuz, while stressing that no decision had been made on any deployment.
South Korea said Friday it was considering "contributions" to US security efforts along the strait  provided that its own military readiness was not compromised.
Iran has warned that any South Korean deployment would be "regarded as direct support for the party responsible for that aggression and will have serious consequences."
Jung Kyung-jik of the civic group People's Solidarity for Participatory Democracy told AFP that he saw Tehran's point.
"As Iran has said, the deployment of our troops to the region would amount to direct participation in an illegal war," he said.
"There have been numerous violations of international law arising from US attacks on Iran, including the bombing of an elementary school and energy infrastructure," he said.
Trump has struggled to get help from allies in the war that the United States and Israel launched on Iran six months ago and has since hit an impasse.
Iran maintains a stranglehold on the strategic strait – which was the conduit for one-fifth of the world's oil supply before the war – and Washington has pressed its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
Choi Young-ok, a member of Korean Peace Solidarity for Sovereignty and Reunification, warned that a deployment would "inevitably lead to casualties."
"Sending our troops to an illegal war waged by the United States is unacceptable," she said.
"There is no reason for us to send troops when no other country has done so or said it would."
If Seoul were to deploy armed forces to the strait, it would require parliamentary approval by a majority vote in the National Assembly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC: Abdul Azeez chose to remain in purple lock-up attire, handcuffs for court appearance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim chose to wear purple police lock-up attire and handcuffs when he appeared in the Sessions Court here today, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said.
In a statement, the MACC said its officers, the police escorting Abdul Azeez and his lawyer had advised him to change into ordinary clothes before he was taken to court.
“He was also informed that there was no need for him to wear handcuffs,” it said.
However, the MACC said Abdul Azeez insisted on remaining in the lock-up attire and handcuffs until the charge against him had been read.
The commission said that no party, particularly the MACC, had instructed or required him to appear in that manner.
It also urged the public not to speculate or circulate inaccurate information concerning the matter.
Abdul Azeez pleaded not guilty today to using his position as TH chairman to secure the chairmanship of Putrajaya Perdana Berhad and influence TH’s board to approve an investment of up to RM193.5 million in the company in 2014.
He was separately remanded for two days today alongside two former senior TH officials to assist a police investigation into alleged cheating involving the pilgrim fund’s hibah payments.

Title: Cabinet expresses condolences to families of five killed in Sarawak FDS helicopter crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The Cabinet today expressed its condolences to the families of the five victims who died in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak, yesterday.
Unity government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and all ministers offered their sympathies and condolences at the weekly Cabinet meeting today.
“At present, the investigation process is ongoing and the Cabinet will be updated on its progress later," he said at a press briefing broadcast live after the Cabinet meeting in Putrajaya today.
Fahmi, who is also the communications minister, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad had earlier announced the identities of all five victims.
He said the victims’ respective next of kin had been informed of the tragedy.
Fahmi also said the Cabinet had yet to discuss extending assistance to the victims’ families.
“Any further information regarding assistance to the next of kin would be referred to the Health Ministry,” he said.
Yesterday, a German-made MBB BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching, while conducting an FDS operation.
It was reported that CAAM received notification of the crash at 3.58pm.
The pilot, a medical officer, an assistant medical officer and two nurses on board the light, twin-engine, multipurpose utility helicopter were killed.

Title: Malaysian woman held at Delhi airport with 15kg cannabis worth RM2.2m
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — A Malaysian woman was arrested by Indian authorities after she was caught attempting to smuggle 15 kilogrammes of cannabis, valued at approximately 52.5 million rupees (RM2.2 million), at Indira Gandhi International Airport on Sept 4.
Delhi Customs (Airport & General) in a statement on X said the passenger, who arrived from Kuala Lumpur on flight OD-205, was intercepted at Terminal 3 based on profile-based targeting.
"She was diverted at the Green Channel for further inspection. An examination of her trolley bag led to the discovery of 30 polythene pouches containing suspected ganja (cannabis) weighing 15,015.5 grammes (net weight)," the department said.
The suspect was subsequently arrested under Section 43(B) of India’s Narcotics Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, while the illicit drugs were seized under Section 43(A) of the same law.
A case was registered against the Malaysian national under Sections 8, 20, 23, and 29 of the NDPS Act, which deal with the illegal possession, transport, import, and conspiracy involving narcotic substances.  — Bernama

Title: Businessman sentenced to 30 years’ jail, 24 strokes for trafficking more than 77kg of meth
Article:
IPOH, Sept 9 — A businessman was sentenced to 30 years in prison and 24 strokes of the cane by the High Court here today after being found guilty of two counts of trafficking more than 77 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine five years ago.
Judge Datuk Abdul Wahab Mohamed handed down the sentence to Liew Wan Wah, 46, after finding that the defence had failed to raise reasonable doubt at the end of the defence case.
The court sentenced him to 30 years in prison and 12 strokes of the cane for the first and second counts respectively.
However, the court ordered that both sentences run concurrently from the date of arrest, while the cane sentence was 24 strokes.
According to the first charge, Liew is accused of distributing 74,477.8 grammes (74.48 kg) of methamphetamine, at the Gopeng Toll Plaza, towards the entrance to the highway before the toll payment counter, in the Kampar district at about 7.30 pm, June 23, 2021.
For the second charge, he is accused of distributing 3,267 grammes (3.27 kg) of the same drug in the parking area under the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division Office, Kampar district police headquarters (IPD) at about 2 am, June 24, 2021.
The charge was brought under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code and is punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same act, which provides for the death penalty or life imprisonment life with whipping not less than 15 times.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor Yasinnisa Begam Seeni Mohideen, while the accused was represented by lawyer P. Ravee. — Bernama

Title: Eleven men, including college student, claim trial to armed rioting charge outside Air Itam school
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 9 — Eleven men, including a college student, reportedly pleaded not guilty in the Magistrate’s Court here today to a charge of rioting while armed with objects that could be used as weapons.
According to Utusan Malaysia, the pleas were recorded before Magistrate Noor Idayu Salim.
The accused were named as Mohamad Nun Mohamad Jupri, 34; V. Rathakisnan, 22; Soman Sri Mahen Deren, 19; Muhammad Haikal Mohammad Rafiq, 19; Chad Sebastian George Albert, 19; Elijah Yong, 19; Cheow Junnuo, 24; Tony Yen Chun Yun, 19; R. Divagar, 20; Muhammad Amirul Hafiz Abdullah, 21; and Ng Chern Yeow, 24.
The 11 were jointly accused of participating in the riot while possessing objects that could cause harm and be used as weapons at about 2.45am on August 29 outside SJKC Kong Min Cawangan Kedua in Air Itam.
The charge was reportedly framed under Section 148 of the Penal Code and read together with Section 120B of the same law, carrying a maximum five-year jail term, a fine or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Marissa Safina Saiful Adli prosecuted, while Tony Yen was represented by lawyer Edric Loo and the other accused by lawyer K. Mahendran.
The court granted each accused bail of RM6,000 with one surety and fixed October 19 for the submission of documents.
Police previously detained 23 people to assist in investigations into the armed riot.
They said the brawl involved Geng 04 members from different areas and broke out after a discussion over the recovery of a debt failed.
Police said the debt was not linked to illegal moneylending and that two men with no gang affiliation were seriously injured after being mistaken for people involved in the fight.
Police also alleged that a suspect attempted to ram several people with a car during the altercation.

Title: Six civil servants, five agents remanded over alleged falsified documents for illegal vehicle ownership transfers
Article:
IPOH, Sept 9 — Eleven individuals, including six civil servants and five agents, have been remanded for six days to assist investigations into the alleged submission of falsified documents to facilitate illegal vehicle ownership transfers involving 16 registration numbers.
Magistrate Norizan Riduan allowed the remand application, which runs from today until Sept 14, at the Magistrate’s Court here today.
The suspects, comprising seven men and four women, arrived at the court at about 9.15am.
According to a source, the Perak Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) detained them at about 10pm yesterday when they went to the MACC Perak office to give statements.
“Initial investigations found that the alleged offence took place in 2025, with the agents suspected of conspiring with civil servants to submit falsified documents to enable vehicle ownership transfers to be carried out illegally,” the source said.
The documents were submitted to the Road Transport Department (JPJ) in connection with the ownership transfer process. — Bernama

Title: Four killed after car carrying three foreign nationals collides with lorry in Telupid
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 9 — Four people were killed after the car they were travelling in collided with a lorry in Kampung Gambaron, Telupid, about 230 kilometres from here, this morning.
The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre said it received an emergency call on the crash involving two vehicles travelling in opposite directions at 7.28 am.
Seven firefighters from the Beluran Fire and Rescue Station travelled 93 kilometres to the scene, but faced difficulties due to the lack of telephone coverage and Government Integrated Radio Network (GIRN) connectivity.
“Four victims were in the car and were extricated by firefighters, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Civil Defence Force before medical personnel from the Health Ministry (MOH) confirmed that they died at the scene,” it said in a statement today.
The identities and genders of the victims had yet to be established, while their bodies were handed over to PDRM for further action.
The lorry driver sustained minor injuries and received initial treatment from MOH medical personnel before being taken to the Telupid Health Clinic, according to the statement.
The rescue operation ended at 9.58 am after personnel ensured the scene was safe and free from any further hazards.
Telupid is an inland district in Sabah, while Sandakan, the nearest major town, is about 130 kilometres away.
Meanwhile, Beluran district police chief Supt Hasan Majid said the car was driven by a 63-year-old local man who was carrying three foreign nationals, all of whom were killed in the crash.
He said the 44-year-old local lorry driver was injured on his legs and hands, while the four occupants of the car were trapped in the front and rear seats in the incident, which occurred at about 6.30 am at KM7 of Jalan Telupid-Beluran.
“Preliminary investigations found that the car, travelling from Beluran towards Telupid town, is believed to have lost control while negotiating a bend.
“The car is believed to have entered the opposite lane before colliding with a lorry travelling to work from Kampung Gambaron towards Gerak Maju Reality,” he said in a statement today.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 by the Beluran district police headquarters’ Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division.
Members of the public or witnesses with information or dashcam recordings are urged to assist the investigation by contacting investigating officer Insp Alpius @ Nickee Bin Yakim at 019-8707626 or visiting the nearest police station. — Bernama

Title: Another Malaysian pilot arrested over Jakarta drug syndicate probe, says Bukit Aman
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR, Sept 9 — Another local pilot has been arrested to assist in investigations in connection with the detention of a Malaysion co-pilot in Jakarta in July for suspected involvement in an international drug trafficking syndicate.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the Malaysian man, in his 30s, was arrested on Monday (Sept 7) in the Klang Valley.
He added that the suspect was responsible for handling the proceeds of the drug sales.
“So, now we have arrested seven individuals and the suspect (arrested on Monday) is a pilot from another airline,” he told a media conference at an industrial area in Puncak Alam here today.
On Friday (Sept 4), Hussen was quoted as saying that police had arrested six local men suspected of involvement in an international drug trafficking syndicate linked to the arrest of a Malaysian co-pilot in Jakarta in July.
He said the arrests were made based on information obtained from the 39-year-old co-pilot during questioning by an NCID team sent to Jakarta from Aug 11-15.
Media reports previously said the 39-year-old Malaysian co-pilot was arrested by Indonesian authorities at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on suspicion of attempting to smuggle 25 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs.
The Indonesian National Police (POLRI) reportedly found 15 packages containing 70,114 ecstasy pills and methamphetamine, worth an estimated RM45 million.
In a separate development, Hussein said police, based on intelligence gathered, conducted five raids under Op Melanoplus and arrested nine individuals around the Klang Valley on Aug 21.
He said the suspects, including two women, are aged between 19 and 33.
“Police seized various types of drugs, including 61.26kg of methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) liquid, ecstasy pills (0.79kg),  cannabis flower (6.09kg), Erimin 5 pills (3.80kg), cannabis (11.13kg), methamphetamine (3.25kg),  cannabis-laced biscuits (870 grammes), ketamine (490 grammes) and MDMA powder (480 grammes).
“Police also seized 959 cartridges of MDMA liquid, with the total value of the drugs seized estimated at RM10.82 million and weighing over 86kg,” he said.
Elaborating, Hussein said one of the suspects was charged under Section 39A(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 on Aug 28, while three others were charged under Section 39B of the same Act on Sept 3.
He added that three other suspects were placed under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985, while the remaining two were released on police bail. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak govt to channel RM100,000 to each family of FDS helicopter crash victims
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 9 — The Sarawak State Government will channel a contribution of RM100,000 to each family of personnel involved in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, yesterday.
In a statement on social media by the Sarawak Public Communications Unit (UKAS), the state government announced it will also fully cover the education fees of the victims’ children who are still in school through the Sarawak Foundation.
“Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg agreed that the assistance be channelled as a sign of the Sarawak State Government’s concern to help ease the burden of the families and the next of kin involved.
“The full payment of the education fees also reflects appreciation for the sacrifices of the personnel who have provided services to the people, especially the community in the interior,” the statement said.
Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) announced that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals including the pilot crashed near Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport), Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching.
According to CAAM, it received information about the incident from the Flight Information Service at 3.58 pm and the helicopter was conducting FDS flight operations. — Bernama

Title: Hadi calls for abolition of ‘colonial laws’ to make Syariah rule supreme in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has called for the abolition of laws he described as colonial legacies, alleging that these were obstacles to the unfettered implementation of Syariah law in Malaysia.
In the statement, titled “Merdeka: Hapus Undang-Undang Penjajah Yang Sekat Pelaksanaan Islam” (”Independence: Abolish Colonial Laws That Obstruct the Implementation of Islam”), the Marang MP argued that true independence cannot be realised while laws inherited from British rule continue to limit Islam’s position above man-made legislation.
“Colonial-legacy laws must be abolished to ensure the true meaning of independence can be fully realised,” Hadi said in the statement.
“In particular, laws that prevent Islam from occupying its noble position above man-made laws not sanctioned by Allah SWT, due to their many weaknesses that spread wrongdoing, must be removed.”
Hadi singled out several statutes for criticism, chief among them the Syariah Courts (Criminal Jurisdiction) Act 1965 (Act 355), which caps Syariah court sentencing at three years’ jail, a RM5,000 fine and six strokes of whipping — a limit known as the “3:5:6” formula introduced in a 1984 amendment.
He also referenced the Civil Law Act 1956 and the division of powers under the Ninth Schedule of the Federal Constitution, which restricts state legislatures to enacting only religious offences under the State List while criminal law generally falls under the Federal List.
The PAS president argued these constraints prevent state Syariah courts from imposing punishments he described as consistent with Islamic legal tradition, and that overlapping jurisdiction between state and federal criminal law has repeatedly led to state Islamic enactments being challenged in court.
To bolster his argument, Hadi invoked the late Islamic law scholar Ahmad Ibrahim, citing his call for Article 3(1) of the Federal Constitution to be interpreted broadly — encompassing law, politics and economics as al-din, or a complete way of life, rather than a narrow, ritual-bound “religion of the Federation.”
Hadi said this position was shared by several former judicial figures, including ex-Chief Justice Tun Salleh Abas and Tun Ahmad Fairuz.
The statement also traced the historical debate over Islam’s constitutional status back to the 1956 Reid Commission, which drafted Malaysia’s independence constitution.
Hadi noted that an early draft had included language affirming Malaya would remain a “secular state” alongside recognising Islam as the federation’s religion — wording that was ultimately dropped following objections from the Malay Rulers and, later, PAS itself, which argued the eventual compromise in Article 3 was merely “ornamental.”
Much of the statement was also devoted to criticising the DAP, which Hadi accused of blocking further Islamisation of the legal system. He cited the DAP’s party constitution, which describes the 1957 Federal Constitution as a “secular” document, and noted that secretary-general Anthony Loke has said the party will not amend this founding position.
Hadi accused the DAP of leading opposition to Hadi’s own past private member’s bill to raise Act 355’s sentencing limits — a proposal that, in earlier iterations, sought to raise the caps to 30 years’ imprisonment, a RM100,000 fine and 100 strokes of whipping.
He further claimed PAS’s former coalition partners, PKR and Amanah, had failed to defend the Islamic position against DAP on the issue.
Hadi’s statement went further to declare that PAS considers the matter one of religious principle rather than ordinary politics, saying the party has severed political cooperation (tahaluf siyasi) with parties it says challenge Islam’s constitutional standing.

Title: Guan Eng submits ‘Malaysia Agenda 12’ package to Anwar, proposes RM25b in interest-free MSME loans
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has formally submitted a 12-point proposal to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim aimed at promoting economic prosperity and strengthening national unity ahead of Malaysia Day.
In a hand-delivered letter yesterday, the DAP adviser proposed RM25 billion in interest-free and collateral-free loans for 500,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), alongside a one-year interest moratorium on their existing bank loans.
“The banking industry can afford to bear the cost of the interest moratorium on existing MSME loans for one year,” he said.
Lim estimated that financing the interest-free loans would cost RM1 billion annually at a 4 per cent interest rate, citing the banking industry’s RM54.8 billion profit before tax in 2025 — a 13.5 per cent increase from 2024.
He also proposed giving non-Bumiputera communities an amount equivalent to 10 per cent of government allocations for Bumiputeras without reducing existing Bumiputera funding.
“A special taxpayers’ tribunal should also be established for individuals and MSMEs, while individual tax relief should be increased by RM3,000 to RM12,000,” he said.
Lim also urged Putrajaya to immediately return 40 per cent of the net revenue derived from Sabah annually as a special grant and provide Sarawak with an equitable grant in accordance with the Federal Constitution.
He called for the autonomy safeguards contained in Sarawak’s 18-point agreement and Sabah’s 20-point agreement to be implemented to strengthen national integration with Peninsular Malaysia.
Other proposals included approving additional foreign workers, digitising their applications and visa approvals, and abolishing the mandatory 2 per cent Employees Provident Fund contribution for foreign workers.
Lim also called for a review of the expanded Sales and Service Tax, measures to encourage purchases of local goods and changes to SST imposed on raw materials used by the steel industry.
His final proposal was a standardised examination for admission to public universities to replace the separate STPM, foundation and matriculation assessments.

Title: Negeri Sembilan royal dispute: Rembau Undang says MB sign-off cannot validate flawed proclamation
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — Rembau Undang Dato’ Sedia Raja Haji Hassan bin Haji Ab. Hamid today said the Menteri Besar’s signature could not validate a proclamation concerning the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan if the process leading to it was flawed.
In a statement, Hassan said the main question was not whether the proclamation existed or how many people had signed it, but whether the process complied with the Negeri Sembilan Constitution and Adat Perpatih.
“The royal institution cannot be changed through shortcuts. A proclamation is not a substitute for the strict process laid down by the state constitution,” he said.
He said Article 10(1) of the state constitution required a full and complete inquiry before any recommendation could be made for Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir to abdicate as Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
“Was a full and complete inquiry conducted? Was Tuanku Muhriz given the right to be heard? And did those making the decision have the lawful authority?” he asked.
Hassan also questioned whether several individuals who reportedly signed the proclamation had the lawful authority to do so as members of the Undang Yang Empat.
In Rembau’s case, he maintained that Haji Abdul Rahim Yasin had never been proclaimed the 22nd Undang of Rembau, while he himself was proclaimed to the position on June 27.
Hassan said Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim’s claim that he was forced to sign the proclamation and subsequently lodged a police report should also be taken seriously.
He added that the Menteri Besar’s signature alone could not correct or conceal any fundamental flaws in the earlier process.
“Until these fundamental questions are resolved through lawful constitutional and legal channels, no party should act as though a lawful and complete change in the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar has taken place,” he said.
Hassan called on all parties to respect the state constitution, Adat Perpatih, the rule of law and the dignity of the royal institution.

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB says he signed proclamation on Tuanku Muhriz under duress, files police report
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today confirmed that he signed a proclamation concerning the position of Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, but said he had done so unwillingly and under duress.
In a statement, Ismail said he lodged a police report at about 6pm yesterday to enable the authorities to investigate the matter.
“The state government maintains that the Instrument did not comply with the processes and procedures stipulated under Article 10 of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959,” he said.
“It is therefore invalid, unconstitutional and unenforceable,” he added.
Ismail said the state executive council also discussed establishing a reconciliation committee during its meeting yesterday.
He said the committee would serve as a platform to resolve the customary dispute harmoniously and prudently in the spirit of consensus.
Ismail also cited Article 71 of the Federal Constitution, saying the provision requires the Federation to safeguard the constitutional rights and position of a state Ruler.
He reiterated his full support and unwavering loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz as the “one and only legitimate and sovereign” Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
His statement followed claims by four individuals identifying themselves as the Undang Yang Empat, together with the Tunku Besar of Tampin and Dato’ Shahbandar of Sungei Ujong, that he signed the proclamation at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on August 3.
The group claimed that the proclamation was intended to give effect to an earlier declaration concerning Tuanku Muhriz’s position that the four Undangs purportedly signed and sealed on April 19.
The state government did not recognise the April 19 declaration, whose validity remains disputed.

Title: Former childcare assistant charged with abusing two-year-old boy at Mentakab centre
Article:
TEMERLOH, Sept 9 — A former childcare assistant was charged at the Sessions Court here today with abusing a two-year-old boy at a childcare centre in Mentakab last month.
Nor Ain Ashikin Husin, 26, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read out before Judge Jamaludin Mat.
According to the charge, she allegedly abused the child in a manner that could have caused emotional injury at a childcare centre in Taman Keramat Indah, Mentakab, at about 9.45am on Aug 11.
She was charged under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which carries a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment of up to 20 years, or both, upon conviction.
The prosecution offered bail of RM10,000 with one surety, but the defence sought a lower amount, citing that the accused was no longer employed and the surety could only provide RM5,000.
Judge Jamaludin allowed bail at RM5,000 with one surety and set Oct 14 for mention. She was also barred from interfering with the victim or prosecution witnesses pending disposal of the case.
Previously, police confirmed receiving a report over the alleged assault after a video of the incident went viral on social media. — Bernama

Title: Police uncover RM2.4b drug operation in Puncak Alam, seize 13.17 tonnes in biggest haul this year
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR, Sept 9 — Police have crippled a drug processing and distribution syndicate and uncovered a drug laboratory in Puncak Alam here through Op Eumenes conducted in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur, with the total drugs seized estimated to be worth RM2.4 billion on Aug 15.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said three local men and a foreign man and woman, aged between 29 and 43, were arrested in six separate raids conducted around Kuala Lumpur and Selangor.
“During the raids, we seized various types of drugs weighing an estimated 13.17 tonnes, including cannabis, Erimin 5, ketamine, yaba and methamphetamine, as well as various machines and equipment believed to have been used to process drugs at the premises in the industrial area,” he said at a press conference at an industrial area in Puncak Alam here today.
Elaborating, Hussein said the total value of the drugs seized was estimated at RM2.4 billion, making it the biggest drug seizure believed to have been recorded this year.
He said the syndicate, which is believed to have been active since February, used a modus operandi of obtaining drug supplies and processing equipment believed to have been brought in from China before being smuggled into Malaysia.
Police also found a container inside the drug laboratory premises which is believed to be linked to the syndicate’s modus operandi of bringing in materials and equipment from overseas.
Meanwhile, he said police believed the syndicate leader was an individual who was shot dead in a previous raid in Seremban.
He said the individual was believed to have managed the rental of the premises, the entry of precursor materials (chemical compounds) and equipment from overseas, as well as recruitment of syndicate members.
The media had previously reported that police crippled a drug processing syndicate believed to be producing methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) worth RM27.5 million through Op Thrips in Seremban and Kuala Lumpur on Sept 6.
Meanwhile, Hussein said one of the suspects, a Taiwanese, was believed to have acted as the syndicate’s chemist and had entered the country four times.
“We are still investigating the possibility that the syndicate has a network in Taiwan and will cooperate with the authorities there,” he said.
Several syndicate members had yet to be arrested, including one who was believed to have fled the country, while investigations were also underway to determine whether there was any possible involvement of insiders from other agencies.
“All the suspects were charged in court under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 on Aug 21 and 27.
Meanwhile, Hussein also revealed that the syndicate was believed to be linked to a kidnapping victim in Selangor in July.
On July 18, the media reported that police had rescued a man who was kidnapped within 48 hours and arrested six individuals, including a woman, who were believed to have demanded RM7 million in ransom in a special operation at a residential unit in the i-City area, Shah Alam, Selangor. — Bernama

Title: Perak rejects claim Taiping Hospital has no house officers, says 93 currently undergoing training
Article:
IPOH, Sept 9 — Perak has denied an allegation that Taiping Hospital has no house officers (HOs), describing the claim in an article published by CodeBlue as inaccurate.
Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the hospital currently has 93 house officers out of 231 training slots allocated, giving it a 40.3 per cent placement rate.
He said the figure meant there was a shortfall of 138 house officers against the available training slots, but stressed that it was incorrect to claim that the hospital had none.
“We accept the fact that we have filled only 40.3 per cent of the housemanship slots. That is the fact, but to say there are zero house officers is not the truth,” he told a press conference on the sidelines of the State Legislative Assembly sitting here.
Sivanesan said he had met the Taiping Hospital director and obtained clarification on the hospital’s current staffing situation.
According to the hospital, there are currently 219 medical officers (MOs) serving there, comprising 137 permanent MOs, 62 contract MOs and 20 MOs who have completed their housemanship training.
He said another 46 MO positions remained unfilled based on the hospital’s current operational requirements, which include patient management, receiving referral cases from hospitals within the northern Perak cluster and managing acute patient admissions.
“The optimum requirement for medical officers at Hospital Taiping is estimated at 273,” he said.
On housemen, Sivanesan said they could not be placed in every department and were currently confined to six departments.
“At every specialist hospital, we have housemen, but they are confined to six departments,” he said.
Sivanesan said the CodeBlue article appeared to have used photographs from Taiping Hospital’s official Facebook page, which were posted on August 13.
He said the hospital’s Facebook post contained only photographs and did not include any written statement claiming that the hospital had zero housemen.
He said the article was based on a letter submitted to CodeBlue by an individual expressing exhaustion and concern over patients.
“I am not saying everything contained in the article is untrue. I am not saying all of it is wrong. There are truths in it which we will look into,” he said.
However, Sivanesan urged the publication to verify facts with the relevant authorities before publishing reports concerning healthcare matters, saying such reports could cause unnecessary alarm among the public.
“But please, when it comes to health, ensure that you get the facts right. You can meet me. I was not consulted. You can meet the director, who was also not consulted,” he said.
“Get the feedback from the director. We have nothing to hide. This involves health,” he added.
Sivanesan said he respected CodeBlue and acknowledged that the publication had highlighted issues that could be taken into consideration and addressed.
“I have high respect for CodeBlue. They have pointed out certain things which will be taken into consideration and addressed.
“But next time, verify the facts in total before coming out with articles,” he said.

Title: King, Queen extend condolences to families of Sarawak helicopter crash victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia have expressed their condolences to the families of the pilot and Ministry of Health (MOH) personnel who died in a helicopter crash in Sarawak, yesterday.
Their Majesties also prayed that the entire family and next of kin of the victims be given strength and fortitude in facing the loss of their loved ones.
“We extend our Al-Fatihah and condolences to all members of the victims’ families. Their services and sacrifices will always be remembered,” said the King and Queen through a post on the Facebook of Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar today.
Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) in a statement announced that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals including the pilot crashed near the Long Lellang Short Runway Airport (STOLport), Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching, Sarawak.
CAAM received information about the incident involving the helicopter from the Flight Information Service at 3.58pm.
The Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter that took off from Miri was carrying five victims, consisting of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, an assistant medical officer (PPP) and two nurses, all of whom were on official duty. — Bernama

Title: Report: Najib’s clemency bid expected to be discussed by Pardons Board this week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application for clemency when it meets this week, according to sources cited by
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT).
FMT
reported that sources familiar with the matter said Najib’s application was expected to be among the issues raised at the board’s meeting, although it remained unclear whether the meeting would result in a decision or merely a discussion.
A separate source told the online news portal that Najib could potentially be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, although it was unclear whether the option would be considered at the meeting.
The development comes as Pakatan Harapan
(PH) reiterated that individuals convicted of corruption or abuse of power, particularly in high-profile cases, should serve their sentences in full.
In a statement issued after midnight by its secretariat council, PH said it supported the Madani government’s efforts to combat corruption, leakages and abuse of power.
It said those convicted of corruption or abuse of power must fully serve the sentences imposed by the courts, while ongoing judicial processes should be allowed to run their course without creating any perception of outside influence.
The coalition did not name Najib or any specific case in the statement.
FMT reported that the statement came amid reports that the Pardons Board was expected to meet on Sept 11 to consider several matters, including Najib’s pardon application relating to his convictions linked to the 1MDB scandal.
Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine. He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
The Pardons Board subsequently halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
On Dec 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. Najib later withdrew his appeal against the decision.
FMT also reported that it had sought comments from Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh, Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar and Najib’s lawyer Shafee Abdullah.

Title: Dzulkefly: Rescue teams begin evacuation of Long Lellang helicopter crash victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Rescue teams are working to evacuate victims of the helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak, with the operation beginning at 7.30 am today, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said.
He said the operation was being carried out by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM).
Dzulkefly said hospitals in Miri were also fully prepared at all levels to receive the victims once they were evacuated from the crash site.
“As of this morning, the evacuation operation is being carried out by the rescue teams, namely the Royal Malaysia Police and the Fire and Rescue Department,” he told a press conference here today.
Also present were Health director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab and Deputy Health director-general (Public Health) Dr Ismuni Bohari.
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly said the MOH always takes into account input from the authorities on technical and aviation safety aspects before making any decision on the use of helicopter assets for FDS.
He also confirmed that the healthcare personnel who died in the helicopter crash were carrying out routine FDS duties when the incident occurred.
Meanwhile, when asked about flight approval for FDS operations, Dr Mahathar said every movement of an aircraft or helicopter must comply with the prescribed safety procedures before permission to fly is granted.
He said the decision on whether a flight is allowed to operate is subject to approval by the relevant agencies and does not fall under the jurisdiction of the MOH.
“Whether permission to fly is granted or not is subject to approval by the relevant agencies, not the MOH,” he said.
Elaborating, Dr Mahathar explained that FDS operations comprise several components, including scheduled services carried out periodically according to the needs of residents in rural areas, as well as emergency medical evacuation (medevac) services to transport critically ill patients for treatment.
He said medevac missions would continue to be carried out whenever there was an urgent need to transport patients, subject to flight approval after taking into account safety assessments and prevailing weather conditions.
“However, as for scheduled services, the MOH will review the matter and, from time to time, provide input to the team on the ground,” he said.
A pilot and four MOH personnel were confirmed dead after the BO-105 flying doctor services helicopter they were travelling in crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram, Sarawak, yesterday. — Bernama

Title: Rapid KL to begin Kelana Jaya Line track replacement works on Sept 13
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Rapid KL will begin phased track replacement works on the Kelana Jaya Line from Sunday, with affected stations starting services at 9.30am on designated Sundays instead of the usual 6am.
The works involve replacing existing tracks with new ones, along with related maintenance activities to ensure the line’s infrastructure remains safe and reliable.
The track replacement will be carried out in seven phases and is expected to be fully completed by September 2027.
Rapid KL said areas with long curved track sections require more time for replacement, with works on the specified dates extending into the morning to allow the work to be completed properly.
The affected stations and dates are:
Phase 1: Sept 13, 20 and 27, 2026 — Taman Melati and Gombak
Phase 2: Nov 15, 22 and 29, 2026 — Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum
Phase 3: Jan 10, 17 and 24, 2027 — Dato’ Keramat, Jelatek and Setiawangsa
Phase 4: March 14, 21 and 28, 2027 — Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum
Phase 5: May 9, 16 and 23, 2027 — Masjid Jamek, Dang Wangi, Kampung Baru, KLCC and Ampang Park
Phase 6: July 11, 18 and 25, 2027 — Taman Jaya, Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum
Phase 7: Sept 12, 19 and 26, 2027 — Taman Melati and Gombak
Rapid KL said trains at stations not affected by the track replacement works would operate as usual according to their daily operating schedules.
At affected stations, ticket machines will be temporarily unavailable until 9.30am, although passengers can purchase tickets at station counters. Rapid KL and Touch ‘n Go product users can continue their journeys as usual.
Free shuttle buses
Rapid KL will provide free shuttle buses connecting the affected stations throughout the track replacement works to help passengers continue their journeys.
Station staff, auxiliary police and Prasarana Troopers will also be stationed at the affected and relevant interchange stations to assist passengers.
Signboards and information leaflets will be provided as additional guidance.
Rapid KL advised Kelana Jaya Line passengers, particularly those travelling on the affected Sunday mornings, to check for the latest information on the work schedule, affected stations and alternative services via myRapid or Rapid KL’s official social media channels.
The operator said the track replacement works were necessary to maintain the safety and reliability of the Kelana Jaya Line and support more reliable rail services in the future.

Title: Anwar: Govt to provide assistance, support to families of five killed in Sarawak helicopter crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The government will provide all necessary assistance and support to the families of the five victims killed in a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim gave the assurance in a Facebook post today.
Anwar said he was deeply saddened by the crash involving a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter carrying four Health Ministry (MOH) personnel and a pilot yesterday afternoon.
“My thoughts and prayers, as well as (my wife) Azizah’s, are with the families of all the victims as they go through this extremely difficult time.
“May they be given strength and resilience. I urge everyone to give the families space and refrain from speculation while awaiting verified information from the authorities,” he said.
Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching.
The Health Ministry also confirmed that the helicopter, which departed from Miri, was carrying a medical officer, an assistant medical officer and two nurses on official duty, in addition to the pilot.
Among the victims identified by their families were Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 31, and Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 32. — Bernama

Title: Pilot killed in Sarawak helicopter crash had video call with mother for more than an hour before tragedy, says father
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — A video call lasting more than an hour with his mother on the night before the incident turned out to be the final moment for the family of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 31, who was involved in a helicopter crash in Sarawak yesterday.
His father, Bee Sham Ahmad, 59, said his fourth child of 12 siblings had a lengthy video call with his mother, Zaiton Muda, 59, on the night before the crash.
“He always called us, but the night before yesterday, he had a video call with his mother for more than an hour and a half, from 10 pm until after 11 pm... little did we know that it would be his last call.
“We only learned the sad news from my eighth child, who informed us that his brother had been involved in the crash yesterday afternoon,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Bee Sham said the last time they met was during the recent Negeri Sembilan State Election, when his son took a week’s leave to return to Senawang to vote before returning to Miri to resume his duties.
Meanwhile, he said the family was on their way to Miri, Sarawak, to undergo deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) testing and related identification procedures, as well as to obtain further updates on the incident.
“We were informed that all the victims are still at the crash site as it is located deep in the interior. We are still waiting for further information on arrangements to bring the remains home and, if permitted, we intend to bury him at the Forest Heights Senawang Muslim Cemetery,” he said.
Zainol Afiq leaves behind a wife and two children, aged six years and 10 months.
Yesterday, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, was reported to have crashed and caught fire near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM), in a statement yesterday, confirmed the incident and said it received notification of the crash from the Flight Information Service at 3.58 pm.
Apart from Zainol Afiq, the four other victims were identified as Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, assistant medical officer Alexson Adit, and two nurses, Debra Moset and Jessie Paya. — Bernama

Title: Perak steps up preparations for Super El Nino expected to last until early 2027
Article:
IPOH, Sept 9 — Perak is stepping up preparations for the Super El Niño phenomenon, with hospitals and clinics given the highest priority for water supplies, including a minimum 48-hour reserve in storage tanks.
Speaking at the State Legislative Assembly, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said the state government was taking the phenomenon seriously, as it could bring hotter and drier weather than usual, particularly during the Southwest Monsoon from May 14 to September this year.
He said the phenomenon was expected to persist until early 2027, prompting the state government to continuously strengthen its preparedness measures.
“Through the State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN), technical agencies such as the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS) and Perak Water Board (LAP) are continuously monitoring and reporting weather forecasts and water levels at major dams.
“This includes Bukit Merah Dam and Sultan Azlan Shah Dam,” he said.
Saarani was responding to an oral question from Bota assemblyman Najihatussalehah Ahmad about the state government’s plans and preparedness for the Super El Niño phenomenon.
On public health, Saarani said the Perak Health Department (JKN Perak) was guided by the Health Ministry’s 2021 Action Plan for Managing Health Risks from Heatwaves.
He said four main strategies had been outlined, namely targeted health advocacy, daily surveillance of heat-related illnesses, haze and waterborne diseases, activation of the crisis preparedness and response centre if a heatwave warning was issued, and ensuring the continuity of health facility operations.
“JKN Perak, together with LAP, gives the highest priority to water supplies for hospitals and clinics, with a minimum 48-hour storage tank reserve.
“This also includes ensuring sufficient supplies of critical medicines,” he said.
In the agricultural sector, Saarani said the state government was focusing on the efficient management and distribution of water resources through major irrigation infrastructure and the mobilisation of mobile pumps for water recycling.
He said structured agricultural areas such as IADA Seberang Perak were being closely monitored due to their reliance on gravity-flow irrigation systems, which could be affected by declining water levels.
“Should the situation become increasingly critical, JPBN, together with NADMA and MetMalaysia, is prepared to coordinate cloud-seeding operations in targeted catchment areas,” he said.
On environmental measures, Saarani said DOE had activated the National Open Burning Action Plan and the Peatland Fire Operations Action Plan.
He said the department was conducting daily patrols at hotspot locations, including during the day, at night and on public holidays.
“The DOE is also using drones for monitoring and enforcing penalties under Section 29A of the Environmental Quality Act (Amendment) 2024, which provides for compounds of up to RM500,000 and fines of up to RM1 million,” he said.
Saarani said DOE was also working with local authorities, the police and the Fire and Rescue Department to prevent open burning that could worsen air quality and pollution levels.
He said DOE was also regularly monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at high-risk locations to allow early warnings to be issued promptly.
He said LAP had activated a phased mitigation plan covering the optimisation of water treatment plant operations, water supply rezoning, mobilisation of water tankers, deployment of static water tanks and the use of alternative water sources.
LAP had also applied for RM2.4 million from the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security for mitigation measures in affected areas.
“LAP is also working closely with the National Water Services Commission through a war room mechanism to proactively manage any risk of a water crisis,” he added.
Meanwhile, Saarani said the Department of Agriculture, together with the Department of Minerals and Geoscience, had updated and activated more than 100 tube wells at strategic locations to provide groundwater for crops and livestock.
He said farmers were also receiving smart agriculture training as a long-term measure to improve water-use efficiency and ensure continued production.
“This includes technical applications involving the Internet of Things (IoT) and modern farm management systems at district agricultural development training centres,” he said.
He said the state government would activate the State Disaster Operations Control Centre under JPBN if necessary to coordinate logistics and emergency water supplies.
“Daily monitoring of early warnings will also continue alongside public awareness campaigns to minimise health risks and enable immediate intervention,” he said.

Title: Former TH chairman Abdul Azeez charged with abuse of power involving RM190m investment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim was charged today with receiving gratification by using his position to influence a decision to invest RM190 million in a company in which he is accused of having an interest.
Azeez was alleged to have directed then TH chief executive officer Tan Sri Ismi Ismail to nominate him as a board member of Perdana Putra Berhad, a subsidiary, and using his position to influence TH’s board members to invest in the said company.
The alleged abuse of power, filed under Section 23-1 of the MACC Act, was said to have been committed on Aug 25, 2014, at Tabung Haji head office on Jalan Tun Abdul Razak here.
The section provides for a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the value of the gratification or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
Azeez, seen clad in purple police lock up clothing and handcuffed, pleaded not guilty and claimed trial, while asserting that the accusation “is absolutely untrue”.
The prosecution had argued that Azeez should not be allowed bail since he is being charged with a non-bailable offence, but noted that the Court still had the discretion to grant bail.
Deputy public prosecutor Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib, leading the prosecution, initially asked for bail to be set at RM1 million with additional terms.
But defence counsel Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad argued that his client’s cooperation with the authorities over the many years of investigations showed he posed no risk of fleeing, and that the bail set should not be punitive.
Sessions Court judge Azura Alwi granted Azeez bail of RM450,000 with the condition that he reports to MACC office once in three months.
Azeez is the latest person to be charged in relation to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji’s mismanagement released in July.
The report flagged 14 problematic investments, including in Putrajaya Perdana that resulted in a RM193.5 million loss.

Title: No hazardous API readings nationwide, but Serian records very unhealthy level
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — No area nationwide recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at hazardous levels due to the haze as of 9 am this morning.
However, the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal this morning showed that only Serian in Sarawak recorded a very unhealthy API of 214.
Meanwhile, 10 areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy readings, namely Samarahan and Kuching with 185 each, Sarikei (174), Sri Aman (173), Miri Industrial Training Institute (ILP) (171), Samalaju (169), Mukah (156), Bintulu (155), Miri (150) and Sibu (102).
In Selangor, Johan Setia recorded the highest reading for the state with an API of 164, followed by Shah Alam (161), Banting (156), Petaling Jaya and Klang (153) and Kuala Selangor (151).
Also recording unhealthy status were Tasek Ipoh and Tanjung Malim respectively (158), Seri Manjung (152) and Pegoh Ipoh (144) in Perak, while in the federal capital it involved Batu Muda (170), Cheras (161) in addition to Putrajaya (157).
Other areas at the same level were Nilai (159), Seremban (154) and Port Dickson (108) in Negeri Sembilan; Bukit Rambai (155), Alor Gajah (152) and Bandaraya Melaka (103) in Melaka; Segamat (155), Batu Pahat (153), Kluang (151) and Tangkak (142) in Johor.
In total, 29 areas nationwide were reported to be at a moderate level, while four areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 300 and above as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Gombak Setia assemblyman Hilman acquitted of making TikTok statement capable of causing public alarm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Gombak Setia assemblyman Muhammad Hilman Idham was acquitted and discharged by the Magistrate’s Court here today of a charge of making a statement on TikTok that allegedly could cause public alarm.
Magistrate Nurul Izzah Hasan Basri found that the prosecution had failed to establish the essential elements of the charge under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code.
“In conclusion, the prosecution has failed to establish a prima facie case against the accused at the close of the prosecution’s case. Therefore, the accused is acquitted and discharged without being called to enter his defence. The RM4,000 bail is to be returned,” said Nurul Izzah.
According to the charge, Muhammad Hilman was alleged to have made a statement on TikTok that could cause public alarm and induce any person to commit an offence against public order at 2.09 pm on July 30, 2025.
The video link was allegedly viewed by a police officer from the Commercial Crime Investigation Department at Menara KPJ here.
He was charged under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of two years, or a fine, or both, upon conviction.
At today’s proceedings, the accused was represented by lawyers Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali and Nur Mustanir Md Nor, while the prosecution was conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutor Nurul Farhanah Arul Hisham. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan MB: Doctor killed in Sarawak helicopter crash dedicated to serving rural communities
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 9 — Kelantan has lost a Kota Bharu-born, the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, who passed away while carrying out her mission through the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) for the rural communities of Sarawak.
Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud said the official confirmation of the deceased’s passing was heartbreaking when she was serving to bring treatment and hope to those in need.
“The deceased had devoted her knowledge and services far in the rural areas for the sake of humanity. Her passing was a big loss to Kelantan.
“My condolences to the entire family of the victim involved. May Allah SWT have mercy on the deceased, accept all her services as good deeds and place her among the righteous. Al-Fatihah,” he said in a post on his official Facebook page, last night.
Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) in a statement announced that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals including the pilot crashed near the Long Lellang Short Runway Airport (STOLport), Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching, Sarawak.
According to CAAM, the helicopter was conducting an FDS operation at the time of the incident.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad was reported to have said that the helicopter that departed from Miri was operated by a pilot and carried a medical officer, an assistant medical officer (PPP) and two nurses who were carrying out official duties.
Meanwhile, Miri Division Resident who is also the chairman of the Miri Division Disaster Management Committee, Galong Luang when contacted confirmed that all five individuals in the helicopter died in the incident at about 3.40 pm.
Apart from Dr Ainul Baraah, the media reported that the four other victims were identified as Captain Zainol Afriq, assistant medical officer Alexson Adit and two nurses, Debra Moset and Jessie Paya. — Bernama

Title: Those convicted of corruption should serve full court sentences, Pakatan says ahead of Najib pardon bid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has maintained that individuals convicted of corruption or abuse of power, particularly in high-profile cases, should serve the full sentences imposed by the courts.
In a statement posted on Facebook last night, the coalition said the rule of law also required ongoing judicial proceedings to be allowed to conclude independently and in an orderly manner.
“Any decision involving high-profile cases must take into account public confidence in the country’s commitment to implementing the agenda,” it said.
PH said previous high-profile corruption cases had damaged Malaysia’s international reputation, while recent efforts had helped rebuild confidence in the country’s institutions and governance.
The coalition also expressed support for the government’s efforts to combat corruption, financial leakages and abuse of power, while reaffirming its commitment to institutional reform.
The statement came ahead of a reported Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting scheduled for Friday.
Sin Chew Dail
y reported that a fresh pardon application by imprisoned former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak was expected to be among the matters considered by the board.
The PH statement did not mention Najib, the application or the Pardons Board meeting.

Title: Former TH chair Abdul Azeez faces police remand proceedings, corruption charge today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim was brought to the magistrate’s court for a remand hearing before facing a corruption charge today.
Datuk Abu Bakar Isa Ramat, Azeez’s lawyer, said the Umno leader was arrested by the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department yesterday afternoon before being taken to the Dang Wangi police station.
Azeez, a member of Umno’s supreme council, had already been detained by the Malaysian Anti Corruption Commission for seven days, which ends today.
He is expected to face several corruption charges in relation to the Royal Commission of Inquiry’s findings that found mismanagement and fraudulent practices among the fund’s top executives.
News reports of Azeez’s arrest by the police yesterday suggested he is being investigated under the Anti Money Laundering Act. The police was granted a two day remand order that ends Friday.
Azeez’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad was quoted by
The Star
as saying the remand order was also issued against a former TH group chief executive officer and a former group chief financial officer.
Azeez is among several top executives to have been charged in relation to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji’s mismanagement that was made public in July.
The report flagged 14 problematic investments, including in Putrajaya Perdana that resulted in a RM193.5 million loss.
Azeez, then a Umno supreme council member, was TH chairman from 2013 to 2018.

Title: Negeri Sembilan royal dispute: Sungei Ujong Undang says Tuanku Muhriz removal bid invalid despite purported MB sign-off
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — Sungei Ujong Undang Dato’ Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari Meor Ngah today said a declaration purportedly signed by the Negeri Sembilan menteri besar concerning the removal of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, was invalid and could not take effect.
In a statement, Muhammad Faris maintained that the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) had ruled at an earlier sitting that the April 19 declaration concerning Tuanku Muhriz had no legal effect because it did not meet the requirements of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution.
He also maintained that three of the four Undangs involved in the attempted removal no longer had authority as ruling chiefs after losing their customary positions in their respective luak.
“Any matter concerning the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan at present must have our decree in our capacity as Imam of the Undang Yang Empat,” he said.
The statement followed a claim by another group of traditional leaders that Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had signed the proclamation at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on August 3, completing the document first issued on April 19.
The group, comprising the Undang Yang Empat, Tunku Besar Tampin and Datuk Shahbandar Sungei Ujong, called for the proclamation to be enforced immediately.
Ismail, who was sworn in as menteri besar before Tuanku Muhriz on August 2, reaffirmed his full support and loyalty to the ruler on September 6 but did not directly address whether he had signed the document.
At its July 31 sitting, which was chaired by Tuanku Muhriz, the DKU recognised Muhammad Faris as the lawful Undang Luak Sungei Ujong and ruled that Mubarak Thahak, Abdul Rahim Yasin and Maarof Mat Rashad did not have the legal authority to exercise powers under Article X of the state constitution.
The dispute began in April when four individuals claiming to be the Undangs announced Tuanku Muhriz’s removal and named Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the new ruler — a move rejected by the then state government.
